extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners/agents, their counsel, and parties subject to USPTO OED disciplinary processes
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and rules governing signatures, certifications, ethical obligations, and disciplinary sanctions for persons practicing before the USPTO, as applied in an OED Final Order. Includes signature format rules, certification obligations under 37 C.F.R. § 11.18, and sanctions procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: General signature requirement for patent correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: All correspondence filed in the Office, except for a notice of appeal pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 41.31, must include a signature. See MPEP § 502.02 and 37 C.F.R. § 1.4(d).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each piece of correspondence that requires a person's signature must (i) be an original handwritten signature in permanent dark ink or its equivalent, personally signed by that person, or (ii) be a direct or indirect copy (e.g., photocopy or facsimile) of an original (37 C.F.R. § 1.4(d)(1)). If a copy is filed, the original should be retained as evidence of authenticity; the Office may require submission of the original if authenticity is questioned.

rubrics_metrics.name: S-signature permitted formats and limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: An S-signature—i.e., a signature inserted between forward slash marks and not a handwritten signature—is permitted in specified circumstances and has prescribed content and formatting rules (37 C.F.R. § 1.4(d)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The S-signature must consist only of letters or Arabic numerals or both, with appropriate spaces and commas, periods, apostrophes, or hyphens for punctuation, and must be inserted between single forward slash marks (e.g., /Dr. James T. Jones, Jr/). A patent practitioner signing pursuant to §§ 1.33(b)(1) or 1.33(b)(2) must supply his/her registration number as part of the S-signature or immediately below/adjacent to it; the # character may be used only when appearing before a practitioner's registration number. The signer's name should be presented in printed or typed form preferably immediately below or adjacent to the S-signature and must be reasonably specific so the identity of the signer can be readily recognized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Graphic signatures for electronically submitted correspondence
rubrics_metrics.description: Correspondence permitted via the USPTO patent electronic filing system may be signed by a graphic representation of a handwritten signature or a graphic representation of an S-signature (37 C.F.R. § 1.4(d)(3)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Graphic representations used with the patent electronic filing system are treated as permitted forms of signature under the rule; they are subject to the same identity and authenticity expectations as other permitted signature forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification that inserted signature is the signer's own
rubrics_metrics.description: The person inserting a signature under paragraphs (d)(2) or (d)(3) certifies that the inserted signature appearing in the document is his or her own signature (37 C.F.R. § 1.4(d)(4)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A person submitting a document signed by another under the S-signature or electronic signature provisions must have a reasonable basis to believe that the person whose signature is present actually inserted it, and should retain evidence of authenticity. Violations of this certification may result in sanctions under § 11.18(c) and (d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Certifications required by 37 C.F.R. § 11.18 regarding truthfulness
rubrics_metrics.description: By presenting a paper to the USPTO (signing, filing, submitting, or later advocating it), the presenting party represents that all statements made on the party's own knowledge are true, and statements made on information and belief are believed to be true (37 C.F.R. § 11.18(b)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A practitioner or non-practitioner who knowingly makes false or fraudulent statements in a paper filed in the USPTO is subject to criminal penalty under 18 U.S.C. § 1001 and other applicable statutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: 11.18(b)(2) certification elements (improper purpose, lawfulness, evidentiary support, denials)
rubrics_metrics.description: When presenting a paper, the party certifies that, to the best of the party's knowledge, information, and belief formed after an inquiry reasonable under the circumstances: (i) the paper is not presented for an improper purpose; (ii) legal contentions are warranted by existing law or nonfrivolous argument for change; (iii) factual allegations have evidentiary support or are likely to after reasonable investigation; and (iv) denials are warranted on the evidence or reasonably based on lack of information (37 C.F.R. § 11.18(b)(2)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 11.18(b)(1) expressly states that a certification violation may jeopardize the probative value of the filing. Practitioners must conduct an inquiry reasonable under the circumstances supporting the factual assertions in the paper; violations can lead to disciplinary action per 37 C.F.R. § 11.18(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to conduct a reasonable inquiry supporting assertions
rubrics_metrics.description: A presenting party certifies that factual assertions are supported by an inquiry reasonable under the circumstances (37 C.F.R. § 11.18(b)(2)(iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule places an affirmative obligation on the signer/filer/advocate to have performed a reasonable investigation into factual contentions; unsupported allegations or failure to investigate can expose the presenting party to loss of probative value and discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions and disciplinary consequences for certifying false or unsupported papers
rubrics_metrics.description: A practitioner or non-practitioner who violates § 11.18 may be subject to disciplinary action, and false statements can carry criminal penalties (37 C.F.R. § 11.18(d); 18 U.S.C. § 1001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations of signature and certification obligations may result in sanctions under § 11.18(c) and (d) and criminal prosecution where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criminal penalties for unauthorized representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Anyone who falsely holds himself out as recognized to practice before the USPTO in patent matters, or permits himself to be held out as so recognized, or falsely holds out being qualified to prepare or prosecute patent applications, is subject to criminal prosecution and a fine of up to $1,000 for each offense (35 U.S.C. § 33).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This criminal statute operates alongside administrative disciplinary remedies and applies to non-practitioners impersonating or misrepresenting designation as a practitioner.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice (37 C.F.R. § 11.804(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Engaging in acts and omissions that allow another person to sign one's signature to patent filings submitted to the USPTO without consent and without the documents having been reviewed by the signatory constitutes conduct prejudicial to the administration of justice, including conduct prejudicial to the integrity of the federal patent examination and issuance process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitting or enabling others to use one’s S-signature on filings one did not review or authorize is a basis for OED disciplinary action under § 11.804(d), as reflected in the Joint Legal Conclusions of the Final Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practitioner-specific S-signature registration-number requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A patent practitioner signing pursuant to §§ 1.33(b)(1) or 1.33(b)(2) must supply his/her registration number either as part of the S-signature or immediately below or adjacent to the S-signature (37 C.F.R. § 1.4(d)(2)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The registration number may be preceded by the # character only when used immediately before the practitioner's registration number as part of the S-signature; otherwise # is not permitted in an S-signature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence retention and authenticity obligations when filing copies
rubrics_metrics.description: If a copy of an original signature is filed (e.g., photocopy or facsimile), the original should be retained as evidence of authenticity; the Office may require submission of the original if authenticity is questioned (37 C.F.R. § 1.4(d)(1)(ii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioners submitting copies bear the responsibility to retain originals and be prepared to produce them to establish authenticity if requested by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sanctions and remediation procedures used by OED (reprimand, probation, suspension)
rubrics_metrics.description: OED may impose public reprimand, place a practitioner on probation for a set period, or seek suspension for up to twelve months if the practitioner fails to comply with terms of probation or the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Final Order describes agreed sanctions: public reprimand; twelve (12) months probation; practitioner may remain active during probation unless suspended; the OED Director may issue an Order to Show Cause, provide 15 days to respond, and then recommend immediate suspension up to twelve months to the USPTO Director if noncompliance persists. The OED Director may also seek discrete discipline for misconduct forming the basis of an Order to Show Cause.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural publication and notice requirements for discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Final Orders and discipline actions are to be electronically published in the OED's FOIA Reading Room and a materially consistent notice published in the Official Gazette.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Official Gazette notice should summarize the reprimand/probation and the factual basis; the Final Order will be posted publicly at the OED electronic FOIA Reading Room URL provided by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of disciplinary record in future proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may consider the record of a disciplinary proceeding, including the Final Order, when addressing further complaints or as an aggravating factor in future disciplinary proceedings against the same respondent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record may be used to rebut representations by or on the respondent's behalf or to increase discipline in subsequent matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Waiver of rights to reconsideration and appeal in settlement agreements
rubrics_metrics.description: A respondent may waive rights to seek reconsideration under 37 C.F.R. § 11.56, to have the Final Order reviewed under 37 C.F.R. § 11.57, and to otherwise appeal or challenge the Final Order when agreeing to a settlement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A settlement/agreement may include express waivers of procedural rights as part of resolving disciplinary action.
